title: Tabersonine inhibits inflammation and apoptosis through the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway to alleviate LPS-induced acute lung injury.
authors: Ji, Mingxia; Chen, Mengyan; Zhang, Ning
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Tabersonine通过JAK1/STAT3信号通路缓解LPS诱导的急性肺损伤，仅涉及分子对接和湿实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Tabersonine (Tab) holds potential therapeutic value for acute lung injury (ALI), but its mechanism remains unraveled. In order to delve into the mechanism of Tab in ALI treatment, our research group initially conducted a network pharmacology prediction. The GSE225664 single-cell transcriptome data set concerning ALI was downloaded from the GEO database. Differential expression analysis combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis were carried out for identifying ALI-related genes. The drug-related database was employed for the prediction of Tab targets. 28 ALI-Tab targets were predicted through network pharmacology. Core target identification, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and molecular docking revealed that Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) is the potential target and the JAK-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signaling pathway is the potential target pathway for Tab in the treatment of ALI. An ALI mouse model, along with a RAW264.7 cell model, was established through lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation, with Tab administered as an intervention. Cells were pretreated with the JAK1 inhibitor. Lung tissue injury and inflammation was evaluated based on six parameters: (1) lung tissue histopathological features, (2) lung wet/dry ratio, (3) inflammatory cell count in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, (4) total protein concentration, (5) lactate dehydrogenase, and (6) proinflammatory factors. Cell activity was assessed through cell counting kit-8 assay. TdT-mediated dUTP nick-end labeling staining, Western blot, and flow cytometry were adopted to detect apoptosis. Tab pretreatment was proven to be effective in alleviating inflammation in mice with LPS-induced ALI and LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, and suppressing the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway activation. Co-culturing LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 cells with A549 cells led to significantly reduced A549 cell apoptosis. Further research demonstrated that the overexpression of JAK1 significantly inhibit the effects of Tab. The foregoing results prove that LPS-induced ALI is attenuated by Tab treatment, with the underlying mechanism believed to involve the JAK1/STAT3 pathway-mediated inflammation and apoptosis.
abstract_zh: 他波宁（Tab）对急性肺损伤（ALI）具有潜在治疗价值，但其机制尚未阐明。为深入探讨Tab在ALI治疗中的作用机制，本研究团队首先进行了网络药理学预测。从GEO数据库下载了关于ALI的GSE225664单细胞转录组数据集。通过差异表达分析结合加权基因共表达网络分析，鉴定ALI相关基因。利用药物相关数据库预测Tab靶点。通过网络药理学预测得到28个ALI-Tab靶点。核心靶点鉴定、KEGG通路富集分析及分子对接结果显示，Janus激酶1（JAK1）是潜在靶点，JAK-信号转导与转录激活因子（STAT）信号通路是Tab治疗ALI的潜在靶通路。通过脂多糖（LPS）刺激建立ALI小鼠模型及RAW264.7细胞模型，并以Tab进行干预。细胞用JAK1抑制剂预处理。肺组织损伤和炎症根据六项参数评估：（1）肺组织病理学特征，（2）肺湿/干重比，（3）支气管肺泡灌洗液中炎症细胞计数，（4）总蛋白浓度，（5）乳酸脱氢酶，（6）促炎因子。通过细胞计数试剂盒-8法评估细胞活性。采用TdT介导的dUTP缺口末端标记染色、Western blot和流式细胞术检测细胞凋亡。Tab预处理被证明能有效减轻LPS诱导的ALI小鼠及LPS刺激的RAW264.7细胞中的炎症，并抑制JAK1/STAT3信号通路激活。将LPS刺激的RAW264.7细胞与A549细胞共培养，导致A549细胞凋亡显著减少。进一步研究表明，JAK1过表达显著抑制Tab的作用。上述结果证明，Tab治疗可减轻LPS诱导的ALI，其潜在机制涉及JAK1/STAT3通路介导的炎症和凋亡。
